candidates.tradeoff: Preserves8-byte header; all dynamic producers/consumers need element descriptor; views still need a representation discriminator and owner.

candidates.layout: Self-describing16-byte header and packed inline payload; views carry backing owner and data pointer
candidates.tradeoff: Adds8 bytes per owning array and32-byte view objects; offers16-byte inline-data alignment and uniform descriptor-independent width. Prove tiny-array overhead and compiler specialization before choosing.

candidates.layout: Eight-byte owning header with descriptor-directed packed payload; low-bit-tagged24-byte array views
candidates.tradeoff: Keeps ordinary array header size but requires tagged-pointer canonicalization across native physical freeing and poisoning, big-object RC slots, sharing, generated typed destruction and bump/WASM ownership tables. Existing fwp_mem_free writes through the supplied pointer; passing an interior tagged pointer corrupts the free list. Source-only alternative, not compatible without explicit changes.

candidates.layout: Eight-byte owning header with descriptor-directed packed payload; high length-bit flags24-byte view header
candidates.tradeoff: Preserves allocation addresses and ordinary8-byte header. All length readers must mask the flag and all data access must select inline payload versus view data. Reserve bit63 with explicit logical length<=INT64_MAX and checked arithmetic even for packed I8/U8. A view retains one same-element backing Array; view updates copy and cannot reuse backing. Requires all generated/native consumers, SIMD LANES aliases and typed destructors to use helpers. No width or ownership evidence yet.

requirements: I8/U8,I16/U16,I32/U32,F32 use1/2/4-byte storage; I64/U64/F64 stay8 bytes. Signed loads preserve extension; F32 loads preserve low32-bit encoding.
Every producer, callback, copy, equality/order/hash, text/binary/JSON, SIMD,tensor,linalg,foreign boundary and typed destructor must agree.
Packed scalar storage is an unscanned leaf; pointer/boxed payloads retain typed owner handling.
Views flatten backing ownership, validate bounds/offset arithmetic and alignment, and cannot reuse shared backing for mutation.
Inspect bytes, sizeof/offsetof/alignment, ARM/Intel generated assembly, raw/native behavior, GC/reuse controls and requested/live allocation before acceptance.
The108 direct Array references are an initial source map, not complete coverage: alias-based accesses, generated C workers/destructors, literals, parsing and foreign conversions must also be checked.

Preserve interpreter/native array-count and trap-order agreement at allocation boundaries. Keep the existing logical count limit unless an explicit semantic review changes it; natural-width native storage must not silently accept counts that the interpreter rejects.
next: Complete accepted phase2 audit first; choose layout using equivalent workload overhead measurements and then implement every consumer in one coherent representation bundle.

sourceReview.nativeRc: Small RC slots accept interior words and sharing canonicalizes them, but big-object slots accept only object starts. Physical small frees clear memory and insert a free-list link at the supplied address. Low-bit tagging is unsafe unchanged.
sourceReview.wasmRc: Resource counts use exact V keys; native slot behavior cannot be assumed on bump/WASM.
sourceReview.preferredExperiment: Evaluate high length-bit view flag against explicit16-byte metadata header using actual tiny-array/AD overhead and all-width views; choose after phase2 acceptance.

abiPreparation.baseline: Workers currently use V scalar arguments and field-count keyed structs of V fields. Float bit bridges are valid but do not request natural floating-point call/return classification.
abiPreparation.layouts: Keep field-count analysis for escape/flattening decisions, add layout IDs keyed by concrete field MT sequence, and retain V bridges for closures, generic runtime calls, ownership checkpoints and foreign wrappers.
abiPreparation.scalars: Use native C float/double and fixed-width integer scalar worker parameters/results when supported; reconstruct the existing V encoding at the worker body boundary so ordinary typed IR and cleanup continue to agree. Validate exact signed extension and low32 F32 bits.
abiPreparation.records: Use naturally typed C fields in direct-worker aggregate returns/arguments. Same-count records with different MT fields cannot share a layout. Generated result temporaries, field projections, boxing and variant bridges must carry the right layout.
abiPreparation.assemblyCases: Inspect F64 pairs and ARM homogeneous3/4-float aggregates versus mixed float/pointer records on both architectures; C ABI rules determine registers. Preserve separate diagnostic flags from production-performance flags.
abiPreparation.acceptance: Actual sizeof/offsetof/alignment and byte/assembly artifacts, raw/native oracles, ABI/FFI boundaries, exceptional owners and complete allocation/live memory profiles. No register, packing or speed claim from source review alone.

implementationSketch.status: Source-only plan; phase2 actual acceptance required before implementation
implementationSketch.workerBoundary: Derive C parameter/result types from each concrete monomorphic MT. Convert to existing V locals at entry and back at return initially, so Clang can remove bit bridges while existing body semantics and cleanup remain intact.
implementationSketch.layouts: Key aggregate layouts by ordered concrete field types rather than field count. Use natural float/double/fixed-width integer fields and word/pointer representations where ownership requires them. Preserve V-based closure/runtime/foreign bridges unless their explicit ABI contract changes.
implementationSketch.heapRecords: Keep boxed record layout and typed drop behavior unchanged initially; typed worker structs can eliminate temporary boxes without changing the public value model.
implementationSketch.controls: Use exact bit-pattern/NaN/signed-zero and small signed/unsigned controls, generic/callback/FFI/nonlocal exits, sizeof/offsetof/alignment, and ARM/Intel disassembly. Diagnostic no-inline flags must be recorded separately from production performance evidence.
implementationSketch.limits: C ABI determines actual register classes and sret behavior. Do not infer register use from C structs alone or claim wider unverified numeric formats.

typedStoragePreparation.status: Source-reviewed integration proposal; not implemented or validated
typedStoragePreparation.existingDescriptor: runtime/fwp_rt.c fwp_desc already distinguishes signed and unsigned widths, F32/F64 and K_ARRAY.elem; preserve its existing width field meanings
typedStoragePreparation.existingSpecialization: src/cgen.rs ResultOwnership::ArrayOperation builds monomorphic typed wrappers and element Dup/Drop hooks. Extend these wrappers with element descriptors rather than introducing language syntax or conflating numeric width with ownership.
typedStoragePreparation.owningHeader: Preferred experiment keeps uint64 length and naturally packed inline payload; width and scalar decoding come from the concrete element descriptor. F32 uses low32-bit payload encoding; signed small loads must sign extend and unsigned loads zero extend.
typedStoragePreparation.genericBoundary: Every array-producing/consuming primitive, generic foreign wrapper, callback bridge, constant emitter and runtime serialization boundary must carry the same concrete descriptor. An untyped V-word fallback cannot consume a packed array directly; explicit descriptor-aware bridging must preserve value and lifetime semantics.
typedStoragePreparation.views: Use a separate high length-bit view flag, retain one flattened same-element backing owner, and dispatch length/data helpers before reading payload. Keep the existing constructor count bound until a separately reviewed semantic change; this lies below the flag bit. Typed destruction must drop the backing owner once and never treat view metadata as elements.
typedStoragePreparation.acceptance: All producer/consumer aliases, immutable update copies, GC/reuse/unwind, JSON/printing/hash/equality, numeric kernels and FFI must be covered before publishing packed support; exact byte and alignment evidence must precede performance claims.

collectorAndReuse.numericOwners: Allocate naturally packed pointer-free numeric owners as leaf objects when descriptor proves no managed children; allocation must still participate in native counted physical reclamation. Record collector scanning/liveness as well as requested bytes.
collectorAndReuse.viewRoots: View metadata contains a real backing-owner pointer and must remain scanned/rooted until typed destruction releases that owner. Never mark the view header as a numeric leaf merely because its element type is scalar.
collectorAndReuse.immutableUpdates: Exclude view headers from in-place update/reuse. A unique view is not proof that its backing storage is uniquely owned; produce a packed owning copy before mutation unless a separately proved transfer applies.
collectorAndReuse.alignment: The eight-byte owning header provides natural alignment up to eight bytes, not guaranteed sixteen-byte SIMD alignment. Use checked unaligned accesses or explicit stronger allocation/layout proof for vector loads.
collectorAndReuse.measuredSpace: Record requested bytes, actual allocation class, live/count/freed bytes and retained backing size. Header and size-class rounding can change the realized density gain; views can retain more backing memory than their own size suggests.
